1.note: Zechariah is using the phrase translated as **And I turned** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

Zechariah is using **I lifted my eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I looked up.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I looked up]

Zechariah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and look]

1.q: אַרְבַּ֤ע מַרְכָּבוֹת֙ יֹֽצְא֔וֹת מִ⁠בֵּ֖ין שְׁנֵ֣י הֶֽ⁠הָרִ֑ים
1.note: Here, **four chariots coming out from between two mountains** represents the divine agents that Yahweh sends out to execute his purposes in the earth. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could include this information in a footnote. Alternate translation: [four chariots, which represent the divine agents Yahweh sends out to carry out his purposes, coming out from between two mountains]

Here, **mountains of bronze** represents the permanence and strength of Yahweh’s heavenly dwelling place. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could include this information in a footnote. Alternate translation: [represented the permanence and strength of Yahweh’s heavenly dwelling place]

2.note: If your language would not represent numbers in a form such as first and second, you could represent these numbers in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [In the chariot that went at the front … and in the chariot that went after it]

3.note: If your language would not represent numbers in a form such as third and fourth, you could represent these numbers in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [and in chariot three … and in the last chariot]

4.note: The phrase **And I answered and said** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent both terms explicitly.

5.note: The phrase **answered and said** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent both terms explicitly.

Here the angel is speaking as if these chariots were **the four winds of the heavens** meaning that they go in every direction, covering the entire earth. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [four messengers from heaven who will cover the entire earth]
The word translated as **winds** could mean: (1) wind, denoting directions, Alternate translation: [four directions from] (2) spirits. Alternate translation: [four of God’s servants in]

Here, **standing before** represents being ready to serve. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from readiness to serve]

7.note: Zechariah is using the adjective **strong** as a noun to mean a certain kind of horse. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [And the strong horses]

7.q: וְ⁠הָ⁠אֲמֻצִּ֣ים יָצְא֗וּ וַ⁠יְבַקְשׁוּ֙ לָ⁠לֶ֨כֶת֙ לְ⁠הִתְהַלֵּ֣ך בָּ⁠אָ֔רֶץ וַ⁠יֹּ֕אמֶר לְכ֖וּ הִתְהַלְּכ֣וּ בָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ וַ⁠תִּתְהַלַּ֖כְנָה בָּ⁠אָֽרֶץ
7.note: Here, **sought to go** marks **to walk about in the earth** as the goal or purpose of **went out**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

7.q: לְ⁠הִתְהַלֵּ֣ך בָּ⁠אָ֔רֶץ & לְכ֖וּ הִתְהַלְּכ֣וּ בָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ וַ⁠תִּתְהַלַּ֖כְנָה בָּ⁠אָֽרֶץ
7.note: Zechariah is using **to walk about in the earth** as a common expression of the culture to mean “to patrol the earth.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to patrol the earth … Go, walk about in the earth … and they walked about in the earth]
The pronoun **he** refers to the angel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the angel said to them]

The words translated as **Go, walk about in the earth** are imperatives, but they communicate permission rather than a command. If the imperatives do not communicate permission for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates permission. Alternate translation: [Go ahead and walk about in the earth]
The pronoun they refers to the strong horses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the strong ones walked about in the earth]

8.note: The phrase **And he called out to me and spoke to me, saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent all three terms explicitly.
The pronoun **he** refers to the angel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the angel called out to me]

The angel is using the term **See** to focus Zechariah’s attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Pay attention]
The phrase **the ones** refers to the chariots with their horses. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the chariots going out to the land of the north]

The angel is using **have caused my spirit to rest** as a common expression of the culture to mean “have satisfied my anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [have calmed me down]
Here, my spirit represents “my anger” or “my wrath.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [my wrath]
The pronoun **my** refers to Yahweh, who is speaking through the angel. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s spirit]

9.note: Zechariah is using **the word of Yahweh came to me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh communicated a message to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh communicated a message to me]

Zechariah is using the phrase **And the word of Yahweh came to me** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

10.note: The next verse clarifies that Zechariah is to take silver and gold from the exiles. You could include this information here if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Take silver and gold from the exiles]

The implication is that **the exiles** refers to people who had returned from exile in Babylon. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the recently returned exiles]
These are the names of men. This **Josiah** is not the same person as King Josiah.

10.q: וּ⁠בָאתָ֤ אַתָּה֙ בַּ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠ה֔וּא וּ⁠בָ֗אתָ בֵּ֚ית
10.note: If the connection between the phrase **and you, you shall come on that day** and **and you shall come to the house of** is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [and make sure that you yourself certainly go that very day to the house of]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you shall come** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that Zechariah himself is the one who will go to Josiah’s house. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [you yourself shall come]

The pronoun **who** refers to Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers or restructure the verse to clarify. Alternate translation: [for Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah have come from Babylon]

11.q: וְ⁠לָקַחְתָּ֥ כֶֽסֶף־וְ⁠זָהָ֖ב וְ⁠עָשִׂ֣יתָ עֲטָר֑וֹת וְ⁠שַׂמְתָּ֗ בְּ⁠רֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָ֖ק הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֥ן הַ⁠גָּדֽוֹל
11.note: These instructions are to be carried out in sequence: first take the silver and gold, then make crowns, and then place them on Joshua’s head. Your language may have a connecting phrase that you can use to show this. Alternate translation: [And you shall take silver and gold, and then you shall make crowns, and then you shall set {them} on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.]

Placing crowns on the head of Joshua the high priest was a symbolic action by which Yahweh showed that a future king-priest figure would come. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote.
**Jehozadak** is the name of a man, the high priest.

12.note: The phrase **And you shall speak to him, saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

12.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר
12.note: The phrase **Yahweh of Armies, saying** introduces a direct quotation within a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent these terms explicitly.

12.q: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה־אִ֞ישׁ
12.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh of Armies says that there is a man]

Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look]

Here Yahweh is speaking of this future king as if he were a **Branch** growing from a plant. He means that this person will arise from the line of David. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Descendant is his name]
Here Yahweh is introducing Branch as a new participant in the prophecy. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation.

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its subject come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [Branch … he will branch off]

Here Yahweh is speaking of this future king as if he were a plant that would **sprout** from the ground. He means that this person will arise and emerge. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and from his place he will arise]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [and he will build my temple]

13.note: Yahweh is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **he will build** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it is the Branch who will build the temple of Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [And he himself will build the temple of Yahweh]
Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [my temple]

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **he will bear glory** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it is this man, the Branch, who will bear glory. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [he himself will bear glory]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [will be known as great and powerful]

This could mean: (1) Branch will be both priest and king or (2) Branch will be king, and another person will be a priest who will share the royal power. Alternate translation: [There will be a priest upon his throne]

Here, **his throne** represents “his royal authority.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and will sit and rule with his royal authority]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **counsel** and **peace**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [and they will advise each other peacefully]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **counsel** that is characterized by **peace**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and a peaceful counsel]

The implication is that **the two of them** refers to the offices of king and priest. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [between the two offices of king and priest.’]

14.note: The word Helem is the name of a man. This is an alternate form of the name Heldai from verse 10.
The word Hen is the name of a man. This is an alternate form of the name Josiah from verse 10.
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of memorial, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that people would remember]

Storing the crowns in the temple of Yahweh was a symbolic action by which the people showed that Yahweh had promised a future king-priest. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [as a memorial in the temple of Yahweh to show that Yahweh has promised a future king-priest]
Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [in my temple]

15.note: Yahweh is using the adjective **far off** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [People who live far away]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as Yahweh of Armies. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh of Armies, sent this messenger to you]

15.q: וְ⁠הָיָה֙ אִם־שָׁמ֣וֹעַ תִּשְׁמְע֔וּ⁠ן בְּ⁠ק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵי⁠כֶֽם
15.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that these things will only happen if the people obey Yahweh. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [And if you will listen carefully to the voice of Yahweh your God, this will happen]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **listen** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [you will certainly listen]

Yahweh is using **listen to the voice of Yahweh your God** as a common expression of the culture to mean “obey what Yahweh your God commands.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you will obey Yahweh your God]

Here, **the voice of Yahweh your God** represents “the commands of Yahweh your God.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to the instructions of Yahweh your God]
